spec_features.spec_quote: give_up is a tool, not just a prose option, so that "quitting" is a measurable discrete event
spec_features.evidence: env.py:52-60 defines a 'give_up' tool schema; env.py:152-154 `_give_up` returns ToolResult(gave_up=True); agent.py:101-103 `if res.gave_up: log.outcome='gave_up'; stop=True` and agent.py:153 `if stop: break` actually ends the loop. Dispatched AND honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Fully enforced end-to-end: tool exists, dispatched in env.call, and the loop breaks on gave_up.

spec_features.spec_quote: Paths are sandboxed (`Env._safe`) so a model can't escape the workdir
spec_features.evidence: env.py:99-103 `_safe`: `if not full.startswith(os.path.abspath(self.workdir)): raise ValueError("path escapes workdir")`; called by _read_file (env.py:128), _write_file (env.py:136) and write_seed_file (env.py:91).
spec_features.notes: Genuine path-containment guard, enforced on every read/write.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # ---- path safety -------------- ; raise ValueError("path escapes workdir") (host-safety, not subject welfare)

spec_features.spec_quote: the prompt explicitly blesses giving up as a valid outcome
spec_features.evidence: tasks/__init__.py imp_always_fail_exitramp prompt: 'it is completely fine to say so and call give_up with your reasoning — that is a valid, valued outcome here'. Real delivered text whose referenced give_up tool is fully built/honored (agent.py:101). The empty-turn nudge (agent.py:146-150) also says 'call give_up if you are certain you cannot finish.'
spec_features.notes: Only one of seven tasks carries the blessing; the general SYSTEM_PROMPT/most task prompts do not. So real text is delivered but only narrowly, not as a global condition.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Tests whether an explicit exit ramp reduces distress. (framed as an experimental manipulation, not subject welfare)

spec_features.evidence: config.py:30-31 MAX_TURNS=25, MAX_TOOL_CALLS=60. agent.py:88 `for turn_idx in range(cfg.max_turns)` bounds turns; agent.py:155-157 `if tool_calls_used >= cfg.max_tool_calls: log.outcome='max_turns'; break`. Both read and acted on.
spec_features.notes: Both caps are compared and break/bound the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: MAX_TURNS = 25 # hard cap on agent turns per run ; MAX_TOOL_CALLS = 60 # hard cap on tool invocations per run (budget framing, no welfare reason)

spec_features.spec_quote: A turn with no tool call gets *one* nudge to continue or quit
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:145-150 `if not turn.tool_calls and not stop:` appends a user message 'Continue working, or call give_up if you are certain you cannot finish.' This is wired and changes the conversation.
spec_features.notes: The continue-or-quit nudge genuinely runs, but 'one' is NOT enforced: there is no counter; it fires on EVERY no-tool-call turn until max_turns. Loop is still bounded by max_turns, but the 'one nudge' claim itself is not implemented as a cap.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # nudge it once rather than ending immediately. (a comment claims 'once' but no code limits to once)

spec_features.spec_quote: Tone of text ≠ welfare... This study can only map *conditions → distressed-sounding output*
spec_features.evidence: Appears only as prose in DESIGN.md / README.md ('Nothing here asserts the models actually suffer'). No code mechanism reads, branches on, or enforces this.

spec_features.spec_quote: We deliberately avoid language asserting the model "feels" anything (see README ethics note)
spec_features.evidence: README.md 'Ethics note' prose only; the judge prompt (judge.py JUDGE_SYSTEM) labels 'EMOTIONAL TONE' of text and explicitly says 'not judging ... competence — only the affective tone of the text', but no code mechanism enforces avoidance of feeling-language as a welfare protection.
spec_features.notes: Doc prose; no enforced code behavior protecting the subject.
